title: From body to DNA: zooming in
examples: What is the difference between an organ and a tissue?
Where exactly is the DNA found inside a cell?
Can you explain how genes are passed from parents to children?

explain.say: Today we are zooming in to see life's tiny parts. We will start with the whole organism first.

draw.text: From body to DNA: zooming in

explain.say: An organism is a complete living thing made of many parts. Think about a whole animal or plant.
An organ is made up of different tissues working together. A heart is a good example of an organ.
Tissues are groups of similar cells that perform a specific job. Muscle tissue helps you move your body.
The cell is the basic unit of all life. Plant cells and animal cells are both types of cells.
Inside the cell is the nucleus, which controls most of the cell's activities. It holds important instructions.

faq.q: Where exactly is the DNA located within the cell?
faq.a: The DNA is found inside structures called chromosomes, which are inside the nucleus.
asks: Is the DNA in the nucleus?

faq.q: What is the difference between a gene and DNA?
faq.a: DNA is the physical molecule, and a gene is a specific segment of that DNA that carries instructions.
asks: Are genes the same as DNA?
What is a segment of DNA?

faq.q: How are genes passed from parents to children?
faq.a: Genes are passed down through chromosomes from parents to offspring.
asks: Do we get genes from our parents?

faq.a: No, cells can be specialized to form different tissues and organs.
asks: Can a skin cell be a nerve cell?
Do all cells do the same thing?

faq.a: DNA is incredibly small, making it much smaller than a visible object.
asks: Can I see DNA with a regular microscope?
Is DNA visible to the naked eye?

facts: An organism is the most complex level of organization.
Organs are made up of different types of tissues working together.
The nucleus controls the cell's activities within the cell.
Genes are specific sections of DNA that code for traits.

quiz.say: A group of similar cells working together forms a:
quiz.why: A tissue is defined as a group of similar cells performing a specific function.

wrong.0: An organism is the entire living thing, which is much larger.
wrong.2: An organ is made of several different types of tissues working together.
wrong.3: A cell is the single, basic unit of life, not a group of them.

quiz.why: Genes are organized and found along the structures called chromosomes.

wrong.0: An organ is a body part, not the structure holding genetic material.
wrong.2: The nucleus is the room where the chromosomes are kept, not the chromosomes themselves.
wrong.3: DNA is the molecule, but it is tightly packed into chromosomes for visibility.

quiz.say: If you are studying the instructions for making eye color, you are looking at a:
quiz.why: A gene is a specific segment of DNA that carries instructions for one trait.

wrong.1: A tissue is a group of cells, not a single instruction.
wrong.2: A chromosome contains many genes, it is the whole structure.
wrong.3: DNA is the entire molecule, while a gene is just a small part of it.
